raw.assessment: The incumbent appears effective for stable course assignments: 24 such files had seven-minute median handling, a concrete limit on any account blaming CSV export generally. Overall course-set accuracy was 32/40 and median handling 17 minutes, missing both targets. Assignment changes and renames cluster among affected exports, but this does not establish causation or the authoritative intended set. Fast execution alongside long replacement waits suggests a separate delay. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the unsampled split-course case. All observations are stipulated synthetic evidence.

openings.claim: Using current assignments or names to resolve a requested week's courses may explain some apparent omissions; stable course identity plus week-relevant assignment resolution could reduce them.
openings.delta: Make the export's course-set interpretation explicit and test temporal resolution before changing scheduling.
openings.prediction: Against coordinator-agreed intended sets, week-relevant resolution corrects assignment-change discrepancies while unchanged-course results remain stable; rename-only discrepancies distinguish identity handling from assignment timing.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, compare current and proposed resolution for unchanged, reassigned, renamed, and split courses across two centers. Confirm intended sets with consenting coordinators, compare actual CSV contents, test import compatibility and concurrent attendance entry, and reject deployment if effort or hosting exceeds the bound.
assumptions: Historical assignments and stable identities are available or recoverable within six engineer-days.
Coordinator agreement supplies a usable intended-set reference.
All processing stays within the private service and authorized workspaces.

openings.claim: Does coordinator-controlled regeneration reduce active handling enough to affect the target, or does it primarily shorten elapsed waiting?
openings.delta: Separate replacement delay from the measured handling burden before prioritizing a regeneration control.
openings.prediction: If replacement coordination drives handling, immediate regeneration reduces active minutes; if spreadsheet checking or import dominates, elapsed turnaround improves while active minutes change little.
openings.probe: Use two short sessions per consenting coordinator with counterbalanced fabricated replacement tasks. Compare the current request workflow with a simulated private regeneration control; record active checking, requesting, downloading, importing, and elapsed waiting separately. Preserve CSV schema, center scope, and attendance entry.
assumptions: The bounded simulation fits existing resources.
Session timings diagnose components but do not establish the next-40-export success rate.

raw.assessment: Changes correlate with affected exports; causation and historical data availability remain unproved. The excluded split-course center limits isolation evidence. Both hypotheses require feasibility within six engineer-days and current hosting.

openings.claim: Convert course mutations into reconciliation signals: privately record center-scoped course identity, effective date and changed assignment/name; flag affected weeks for coordinator scope review before generating the documented CSV.
openings.delta: Changes associated with omissions become control inputs identifying course/week decisions requiring attention.
openings.prediction: Mutation-assisted review recovers intended courses missed by current-state selection in reassignment and rename fixtures; unchanged cases require no extra review.
openings.probe: In the first coordinator session, adjudicate fabricated intended course sets, including a split. Compare current selection with mutation-assisted selection and time review. Reject implementation if reliable effective dates, identity continuity or nonblocking reads exceed the resource bounds.
assumptions: Mutation capture is inexpensive and permits ongoing attendance entry.
Failure boundary: missing history, ambiguous split lineage or incorrect dates require coordinator resolution; events cannot establish intent alone.
Reconciliation and output enforce center authorization.

openings.claim: Convert replacement requests into executable corrections: an authorized coordinator selects missing or unwanted courses for the specified week inside the private service, directly triggering regeneration with that reviewed scope.
openings.delta: Dissatisfaction supplies scope information and controls regeneration, replacing a delayed request handoff.
openings.prediction: Replacement waiting decreases; handling improves only if selecting corrections costs less than the handling displaced.
openings.probe: In the second session, compare ordinary replacement requests with staged correction/regeneration. Measure correction effort, waiting, import and intended-course accuracy separately; attempt a cross-center course reference and verify rejection.
assumptions: Existing export code accepts authorized selections within resource bounds while attendance entry continues.
The documented CSV remains supported and participant data stays private.
Failure boundary: inaccurate coordinator schedules can yield faster but incorrect files; selections never override server-enforced center authorization.

openings.claim: Resolve requested weeks through stable identities and historical assignments.
openings.discriminator: Reassignment versus rename discrepancies; unchanged baseline.
openings.probe: Compare current/proposed CSVs with coordinator-agreed sets, including split courses across centers.
openings.uncertainty: History/identities may be unavailable; correlation is not causation.

openings.claim: Immediate regeneration may reduce handling or only waiting.
openings.probe: Counterbalance fabricated request/regeneration tasks; time checking, requesting, downloading and importing separately.
openings.uncertainty: Session improvements cannot establish next-40 success.

openings.claim: Mutation signals trigger affected-week scope review.
openings.discriminator: Recover changed courses without adding unchanged-case review.
openings.probe: Adjudicate fabricated reassignment, rename and split sets; compare selection and time review.
openings.uncertainty: Missing history, wrong dates or ambiguous split lineage need coordinator resolution; events cannot establish intent.

openings.claim: Authorized scope corrections directly trigger regeneration.
openings.discriminator: Correction effort versus displaced handling; intended-set accuracy.
openings.probe: Compare request/correction workflows; measure effort, wait, import and accuracy; reject cross-center references.
openings.uncertainty: Inaccurate schedules can accelerate incorrect files; selection must retain server authorization.

post_distill.decision: Probe before choosing. All must preserve private processing/authorized workspaces, documented CSV and concurrent attendance entry; reject implementation exceeding six engineer-days/current hosting. Validate imports and concurrency in fabricated staging. Synthetic evidence; split-course isolation remains unestablished.
